title: Generate and edit images · Level 3
slo: Choose an appropriate Foundry image-generation model for a stated need.

exercises.question_text: What does an image-generation model do?

options.rationale: Correct. Image generation creates a new visual that corresponds to a written description.

options.text: Matches an existing image to text
options.rationale: This describes image analysis rather than image generation. Analysis starts with an existing image and interprets it.
options.better_fit: Use this when you need to describe or classify an existing image.

options.rationale: Video generation produces moving video content. Image generation produces still images.
options.better_fit: Use this when the desired output is a video clip.

options.text: Answers questions about images and text
options.rationale: This describes a multimodal understanding task. It does not specifically create a new image.
options.better_fit: Use this when an uploaded image must be interpreted with written instructions.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Image generation turns a written description into a new image.

exercises.question_text: Which statements describe GPT-Image-1-Mini? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Correct. GPT-Image-1-Mini is a lighter-weight GPT-Image-1 variant. Its design supports cost- and latency-focused needs.
Correct. GPT-Image-1-Mini is more cost-efficient. It is intended for cases where lower cost matters.

options.text: It supports the same core tasks
options.rationale: Correct. GPT-Image-1-Mini supports the same core image-generation tasks as GPT-Image-1. Its main difference is optimization for cost and latency.
Maximum fidelity is not Mini's main focus. GPT-Image-1.5 is the high-fidelity option.
options.better_fit: Choose this priority for high-accuracy branding and design work.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Mini keeps core tasks while emphasizing lower cost and latency.

exercises.question_text: FLUX is a GPT-Image model created by Microsoft Foundry.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The model family could be credited to the wrong organization.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: FLUX was created by Black Forest Labs and is separate from the GPT-Image family.

exercises.explanation: Correct. FLUX is a separate open-source family from Black Forest Labs.

exercises.question_text: Text-to-image inferencing generates visual output from a written description.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: A written design brief would not be recognized as a request for a new image.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Text-to-image inferencing means generating visual output from a written description.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Text-to-image inferencing creates a visual from words.

exercises.question_text: For most new Foundry image projects, the recommended starting model is ___.

parts.text: For most new Foundry image projects, the recommended starting model is

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: A new project could begin with a model that does not match the general recommendation.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: GPT-Image-1 is general purpose, Mini prioritizes cost and latency, and FLUX is a separate open-source family.

exercises.explanation: GPT-Image-1.5 is the recommended starting point for most new projects because it combines high quality with editing support.

exercises.question_text: A retail operations manager needs many simple product placeholders for an internal workflow. The budget is tight and top visual fidelity is unnecessary. Which choices are best? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Correct. Mini is the lighter, cost-efficient option. Its focus matches tight budgets and noncritical fidelity.
Correct. Reduced cost is a central reason to choose Mini. It directly addresses the budget constraint.
Correct. Mini can suit high-volume generation. Many simple placeholders fit that use case.
GPT-Image-1.5 is designed for high-fidelity creation and editing. The manager has said top fidelity is unnecessary.
options.better_fit: Choose this when visual accuracy, alignment, and precise editing outweigh cost.

feedback.intrinsic: The workflow may use a fidelity-focused option despite its budget constraints.
feedback.instructional: When cost and volume matter more than maximum fidelity, Mini is the better fit.

exercises.explanation: Correct. The high-volume, budget-focused need matches Mini.

exercises.question_text: A design lead is selecting a model for a client brand campaign that requires exact details and high-quality edits. Which choices best fit? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Correct. GPT-Image-1.5 is recommended for branding and design work where visual accuracy matters. Its high-fidelity focus matches the campaign.
Correct. Precise editing supports targeted improvements to existing visuals. This directly fits the need for high-quality edits.
Correct. Strong prompt alignment helps preserve requested visual details. This supports a brand-sensitive decision.
Mini is optimized for lower cost or latency when maximum fidelity matters less. This campaign explicitly prioritizes exact details and edit quality.
options.better_fit: Choose Mini for budget-sensitive, high-volume work with less demanding fidelity.

feedback.intrinsic: The client may not receive the expected visual fidelity.
feedback.instructional: When accuracy and editing quality lead the decision, GPT-Image-1.5 is the better fit.

exercises.explanation: Correct. GPT-Image-1.5 matches accuracy-focused brand work.

exercises.question_text: Arrange the parts to form the correct statement.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The model's integration support is not communicated clearly.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Place the model first, followed by the support statement and the supported environments.

exercises.correct_answer: GPT-Image-1 is supported by agent tools and APIs
exercises.explanation: The sentence names GPT-Image-1 first, then states its support across agent tools and APIs. Broad tool support is a distinct GPT-Image-1 characteristic.

exercises.question_text: Which Python SDK feature can generate new images and edit existing images?

options.rationale: Correct. The OpenAI images class provides Python access for generating and editing images. It is used with the Images API endpoint.
A video REST interface manages video jobs and finished video retrieval. It is not the SDK feature for image creation and editing.
options.better_fit: Use this when requesting and retrieving generated video.

options.rationale: An image-analysis request interprets an existing image. It does not create or edit images.
options.better_fit: Use this when an application needs a natural-language response about an uploaded image.

options.rationale: Sora generates video content. It is not the Python SDK feature for static image generation and editing.
options.better_fit: Use this when the desired output is a generated video clip.

exercises.explanation: Correct. The OpenAI images class can generate and edit images.

exercises.question_text: An AI agent builder needs a general-purpose image model specifically identified as widely supported in Foundry tools, the Responses API, and agent tools. Which model should the builder choose?

options.rationale: Correct. GPT-Image-1 is widely supported across those Foundry tools and APIs. That directly satisfies the integration requirement.
GPT-Image-1.5 emphasizes high-fidelity generation and editing. The stated broad integration support is associated with GPT-Image-1.
options.better_fit: Choose this when visual fidelity, consistency, and precise editing are the primary criteria.

feedback.intrinsic: The builder may miss the model explicitly associated with the requested support.
feedback.instructional: Choose GPT-Image-1 for the stated Foundry, Responses API, and agent-tools support.

options.rationale: Mini is the cost- and latency-focused variant. That does not answer the builder's stated integration criterion.
options.better_fit: Choose this for high-volume tasks where reduced cost or latency is the deciding factor.

feedback.intrinsic: The builder may optimize for cost instead of the requested support.
feedback.instructional: The integration-focused choice in this scenario is GPT-Image-1.

options.rationale: FLUX is a separate open-source family from Black Forest Labs. It is not the GPT-Image-1 model identified with the listed support.
options.better_fit: Choose this when an open-source, photorealistic, or stylistically flexible family is needed.

feedback.intrinsic: The builder could choose a different family and lose the requested match.
feedback.instructional: The broad support described belongs to GPT-Image-1.

exercises.explanation: Correct. GPT-Image-1 is the integration-focused choice.

parts.text: FLUX image models were created by

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The model family would be attributed to the wrong organization.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Microsoft Foundry hosts models, but Black Forest Labs created FLUX.

exercises.explanation: FLUX is a third-party open-source image-model family created by Black Forest Labs.

exercises.question_text: Arrange the following steps in order.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: Saving before decoding would leave encoded data rather than a usable image.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: The flow is prompt, generate, decode, then save.

exercises.correct_answer: Provide a text prompt Use image_generation tool Decode returned Base64 Save as PNG
exercises.explanation: First provide the description and request the image. Then decode the returned data before saving the decoded bytes as PNG.
